name: IEC C14 mains inlet
summary: The three-pin socket a kettle lead plugs into. Needs a 27 x 19.5 mm rectangular hole.
source: The C14 mating face is fixed by IEC 60320, and the 27.0 x 19.5 mm snap-in panel cutout with roughly 3 mm corner radii is the same figure across the major suppliers. Modelled here as the plain snap-in version. What is not verified: the flange size and the 22 mm body depth behind the panel, which differ by a few millimetres between makers, and inlets with a built-in fuse holder or switch, which are much deeper than this. Snap-in inlets only grip thin panels, roughly 0.8 to 2 mm, so on a thicker printed panel use the screw-mount version instead: it takes the same cutout plus two M3 holes on 40 mm centres, but its flange is wider than the body modelled here.

keepouts.label: Room for the spade terminals and mains wiring
Room for the mains lead and its plug

electrical.note: Mains voltage. Usually rated 10 A at 250 V AC. The earth pin is the longer centre one and must be connected to any metal panel.
